title: Error budget in Console (MVP) — wire notes / early product thinking
linked_artifacts: Confluence:(draft) Console error budget views + rollout integration spec
Confluence:(draft) Tiered SLO definitions (Hosted vs Dedicated)
Slack: #product console-and-rollouts thread (error budget MVP scope)
content:
Context / why this doc exists
- We need an MVP Console experience for error budgets that (a) makes budget status legible to oncall + product teams, and (b) integrates with rollout workflows so people understand why a rollout was warned/blocked.
- This is not final IA/UX; it’s wire-level notes + product decisions to unblock Design/Eng.

Non-goals (for MVP)
- Building customer-facing SLA pages (handled separately).
- Deep per-tenant reliability analytics for Private (we may show “guidance” but no enforcement initially).
- Replacing dashboards for SRE investigations; Console should link out to canonical SLO dashboards.

Primary users
1) Oncall / SRE
- Needs: “are we burning?”, “what’s the fastest mitigation?”, “what changed recently?”, “who owns this SLO?”, “what’s blocked by policy?”

2) Eng IC / EM shipping changes
- Needs: “will my rollout be blocked?”, “what scope is impacted (tier/region/service)?”, “how do I request override?”, “what can I change safely?”

3) PM (Hosted + Dedicated)
- Needs: “how are we trending vs targets?”, “what do we communicate?”, “what incidents caused burn?”, “are Dedicated pools meeting expectations?”

4) Support/CS (internal)
- Needs: read-only view aligned with policy, with Dedicated/Hosted context + messaging hints (status page trigger guidance)


MVP product principles
- Default to clarity over completeness.
- Always show scope (tier + region + service/route) upfront.
- Always show “what this means operationally” (warn-only vs soft-block vs hard-block) in the UI.
- Always link to (1) SLO definitions, (2) error budget policy, (3) runbook.
- Don’t make users “interpret math”; show “budget remaining” and “time-to-exhaust at current burn” (with a disclaimer).


Information architecture (MVP strawman)
Left nav:
- Reliability
  - Error Budgets (NEW)
  - SLO Dashboards (link out / or existing dashboard area)
- Rollouts
  - (existing rollout pages)

Entry points:
- Rollout detail page: a “Reliability gate” panel should deep-link into scoped error budget view.
- Reliability > Error Budgets: overview landing.


Key concepts we must be explicit about in UI
- Tier: Hosted vs Dedicated (and “Private: informational only” if shown)
- Scope boundaries:
  - Hosted: multi-tenant. Typically scoped by service + endpoint group + region + (optionally) model family.
  - Dedicated: per customer deployment/pool; must avoid cross-customer leakage.
- SLI types that show up:
  - Availability / success rate
  - 5xx rate
  - Timeouts
  - Streaming disconnect rate (Hosted focus)
  - Latency (p95/p99) — note: error budgets generally based on availability-style SLIs; latency appears as “SLO status” but not necessarily budget (depends on final policy).
  - Dedicated pool readiness (Dedicated focus)


Screen 1: Error Budgets — Overview
Goal: Answer “what budgets are at risk right now?” and provide a quick drilldown.

Wire notes (rough layout):
Header
- Title: Error Budgets
- Global filter bar (sticky):
  - Tier selector: [Hosted] [Dedicated]
  - Region: [All] dropdown (us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-central-1, etc.)
  - Time window: 30d rolling (fixed for MVP; optionally show last 7d trend)
  - Service: [All] (gateway, routing, runtime, control-plane, embeddings)
  - Model: [All] (only if within cardinality budget; might be “Model family”)

Top summary tiles (3–4)
- Budget remaining: “92%” + “(X hours of error remaining)”
- Burn status: “Normal / Elevated / At risk / Exhausted” (maps to policy)
- “Fast burn” callout: “Multi-window burn alert active” (if applicable)
- Enforcements active: “Release gates: WARN ONLY” or “Soft-block” etc (pull from policy engine)

Table: Budget status by SLO scope
Columns (Hosted)
- Scope: Service / endpoint group (e.g., “Gateway: Chat streaming”, “Embeddings: /v1/embeddings”)
- Budget remaining (%)
- Current burn rate (1h) + (6h) (if multi-window)
- Time to exhaust (at current burn) — if burn < 1x, show “N/A (not burning)”
- Last policy action: “Gates warn-only”, “Soft-block enabled”, “Protective throttling enabled” (if triggered)
- Owner (team/oncall)

Rows should be sortable by “At risk” first.

Dedicated mode changes
- Replace “Service/endpoint group” with “Customer deployment / pool” + “API surface”
- Explicitly show that rows only include deployments the viewer is allowed to see.
- No “All customers” aggregate unless we’re certain it doesn’t leak.

Footer / help text
- “What counts toward error budget?” link to SLO definition page.
- “What happens when budgets burn?” link to policy.
- “Data delay: metrics may lag by up to N minutes” (need from Eng).


Screen 2: Error Budget — Detail view
Goal: Explain WHY we are burning and what to do next.

URL concept
/reliability/error-budgets?tier=hosted&region=us-east-1&scope=gateway.chat_streaming
(or in dedicated: scope=customer_pool_id + endpoint group)

Header
- Breadcrumb: Reliability > Error Budgets > [Scope]
- Pill(s): Tier: Hosted | Region: us-east-1 | Scope: Gateway: Chat streaming
- “Owner / oncall” contact + runbook button

Main panels
1) Budget remaining over time
- Chart: “Budget remaining (30d rolling)”
- Overlay markers for incidents / rollouts / config changes (MVP: show deploy events if available from rollout tooling; otherwise show last deploy time)

2) Burn rate chart
- Multi-window burn (1h, 6h) vs thresholds
- Show “policy thresholds” as dotted lines (e.g., 2x, 5x, 10x — final numbers TBD)

3) SLI breakdown
- Success rate (or error ratio) chart, with stacked error classes:
  - 5xx
  - timeouts
  - streaming disconnects (server-side)
  - (exclude) client aborts (explicitly shown as excluded)
- Include “Excluded traffic” footnote w/ counts (help debug “why doesn’t this match what my client saw?”)

4) Top contributing dimensions (careful re: cardinality)
- “Top models by error contribution” (if enabled; maybe model family only)
- “Top routes”
- “Top clusters/POPs” (if we have)

5) “What is blocked right now?” panel (critical MVP)
- Status: Normal / At risk / Exhausted
- Policy mode: warn-only / soft-block / hard-block
- Affected enforcement points:
  - Rollouts: canary progression blocked? (yes/no)
  - CI deploy gate: block merges/deploys? (yes/no)
  - Routing mitigation: fallback enabled? (yes/no)
  - Throttling: protective throttling enabled? (yes/no)
- Link: “Request override”

Actions / links area
- Runbook link (error budget exhaustion response runbook)
- “Open incident” (if there is an active incident; otherwise “Start incident” link)
- “View SLO definition” (specific to this SLI)
- “View dashboards (Grafana/Looker)”


Permissions model (MVP)
We need a minimum viable set that prevents Dedicated leakage while keeping internal usability.

Roles (strawman)
- Redwood employee (default)
  - Hosted budgets: view all Hosted scopes.
  - Dedicated budgets: view only Dedicated deployments in your org’s allowlist (team-based) OR if you’re on Dedicated oncall/support list.

- Dedicated restricted viewer
  - Can view a specific customer deployment/pool.
  - Cannot search/browse all Dedicated pools.
  - Cannot see “top customers” lists.

- Support/CS
  - Read-only access, Dedicated restricted by account assignment.
  - Needs “comms hints” panel (see below).

- Admin (SRE / Platform)
  - Can view all tiers + all Dedicated pools.
  - Can create overrides (with TTL + reason).

Open questions for Eng/Sec
- Do we have a reliable mapping from Console user -> customer account assignments (for Support) that is up to date?
- For Dedicated, should scope identifiers in URLs be opaque to avoid guessability?
- How do we audit who accessed a Dedicated customer pool reliability view?


How we present tier context (UI language)
We keep getting confusion like “Dedicated should never degrade” or “Hosted is best-effort.” We need consistent copy.

Tier copy snippets (draft)
- Hosted
  - “Hosted is multi-tenant. During elevated burn, the system may apply protective mitigations (fallback routing, throttling) to preserve overall availability.”

- Dedicated
  - “Dedicated is isolated capacity. During elevated burn, mitigations prioritize pool stability and may restrict changes (soft/hard blocks) rather than shifting load to other customers.”

- Private (if shown at all in MVP)
  - “Private deployments are customer-managed environments. These views are informational and may not reflect enforcement gates.”

MVP UI affordance
- Always show Tier pill next to the scope name.
- Add a “What does this tier mean?” tooltip linking to tier principles.


Rollouts integration (MVP)
Where to integrate
1) Rollout detail page
- Add a “Reliability gate” section:
  - Gate status: Passed / Warned / Blocked
  - Text: “Blocked because error budget exhausted for Hosted • Gateway: Chat streaming • us-east-1”
  - Link: “View error budget details” (deep link to scoped detail view)
  - If override used, show: “Override active until 2026-02-19 18:00 UTC (Reason: …, Approver: …)”

2) Rollout canary step UI
- If blocked, show “Next steps”:
  - “Check mitigation runbook”
  - “Roll back / pause rollout”
  - “Request override” (if permissions)

Override request (MVP outline)
- We may not build a full workflow in Console for MVP.
- Minimal: link to internal form / Slack channel / ticket template.
- But we should display override status consistently if Eng provides an API.


Comms hints (Support/CS read-only panel)
This is optional for MVP but seems high leverage.
Panel on detail view (visible to Support/CS and Admin):
- “Customer impact guidance”
  - Hosted: “If burn is >X for >Y minutes, consider status page update.”
  - Dedicated: “If affected pool is a named enterprise customer, coordinate with CSM + Dedicated oncall; do not post broad status unless multiple pools affected.”
- Link to comms guidelines page.


Metrics/data constraints we should design around
- Cardinality: can’t always break down by model + route + region + customer all at once.
  - Proposed: fixed drill path. Example Hosted:
    - Overview: per service + endpoint group + region
    - Detail: allow model family OR route (not both) in “top contributors”

- Data freshness:
  - Need to show “Last updated at” time.
  - If budget compute job lags >N minutes, show warning banner.

- Exclusions:
  - We must show excluded classes somewhere in detail view (auth errors, invalid requests, client aborts) or we’ll get dashboard mismatch escalations.


Open questions / decisions needed (before design locks)
1) What is the MVP “unit” of an error budget in Hosted?
- per service? per endpoint group? per region? per model family?
- risk: too coarse = not actionable. too fine = cardinality + blame.

2) Latency vs availability budgets
- Policy may treat latency SLOs separately (no “budget” but still alert/enforce?)
- Console should not imply “latency budget remaining” unless it’s actually in the computation.

3) Dedicated pool readiness
- Should readiness be shown as a first-class SLO on Dedicated overview?
- If readiness dips but is short-lived, is it ticket-only vs page? (policy question)

4) Enforcement mode display
- We need a canonical “current enforcement mode by scope” field from policy engine.
- UI copy should reflect warn-only / soft-block / hard-block.

5) Customer-facing views
- Not MVP, but design should not preclude future “customer portal reliability view.”
  - If we do later, must ensure Dedicated scoping and sanitized labels.


Next steps (as of 2026-02-19)
- Sync with Chloe + Kenji on IA and first wireframes.
- Confirm with Aisha/Sergio what the budget service can return (fields, timestamps, supported group-bys).
- Confirm with Jordan what policy engine can return for “enforcement mode” + override metadata.
- Write 1–2 example deep links from rollout pages and validate they’re stable.
- Decide if we ship “Support/CS comms hints” in MVP or Phase 1.5.

Appendix: Example scopes (draft)
Hosted example scopes
- gateway.chat_streaming (TTFT + disconnect SLI; availability SLI)
- gateway.chat_non_streaming
- gateway.embeddings
- routing.core
- runtime.inference

Dedicated example scopes
- dedicated.pool_readiness
- dedicated.chat_streaming (per pool)
- dedicated.embeddings (per pool)
